newsitem.title: USA: Giant Industries to buy 96 Thriftway stores.
newsitem.headline: Giant Industries to buy 96 Thriftway stores.

text.p: Giant Industries Inc on Tuesday said it has agreed to a lease/purchase agreement for 96 retail convenience stores in four western states from Thriftway Marketing Corp. of Farmington, N.M.
Giant, a refiner and marketer of petroleum products, also will buy seven stores under development, and it will acquire Thriftway's petroleum products transportation operation.

Giant will pay $16 million for an as yet undetermined number of stores and for the transportation operations. It will then lease the remaining stores for 10 years with an option to acquire them for $23 million more.
The deal is subject to due diligence and government approval, and it is scheduled to close on May 31.
In a statement, Giant said the deal should contribute about $13 million to earnings before interest, taxes and depreciation in the first 12 months.

"It adds significantly to our goal of achieving further integration between our refining and marketing businesses," said Jim Acridge, chief executive officer. "It will also provide profitable growth and increased economies of scale as we significantly increase the number of company owned and operated service station/convenience stores."

The stores are in New Mexico, Arizona, Colorado, and Utah and are in, or adjacent, to Giant's primary markets. he stations will be operated by Giant under the current trade names of Thriftway, Plateau, Gasman and Gasamat.
Giant is also starting into long-term supply agreements to provide gasoline and diesel fuel to service stations in the area that will continue to be operated by Thriftway.
Fuel sales through company owned or supply-controlled retail units will consume about 30 percent of its two refineries' total production and 43 percent of gasoline production.
